clue.text: Woodcutter seen in a party with a graduate

parts.note: LIB is short for the Liberal party
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate's degree

explanation.surface: A lumberjack is spotted at a party, accompanied by someone fresh from university.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Arabian Nights tale, Ali Baba is a poor woodcutter who stumbles on the forty thieves' cave.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of the Arabian Nights story earns his living cutting wood before finding the thieves' treasure.

clue.text: Feminist writer with temperature in a large bed

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A feminist author lies feverish in an oversized bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here: the pieces run in order, with T added at the end rather than put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott, author of Little Women, campaigned for women's suffrage and is read as a feminist novelist.

clue.text: "Mistaken men, and patriots in their hearts, / Not wicked, but seduced by — arts" (Dryden)

definitions.text: "Mistaken men, and patriots in their hearts, / Not wicked, but seduced by — arts" (Dryden)

parts.words: "Mistaken men, and patriots in their hearts, / Not wicked, but seduced by — arts" (Dryden)
parts.note: a quotation from Dryden's Absalom and Achitophel with one word gapped: the missing adjective, meaning ungodly, describes the arts that led the rebels astray

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: the solver supplies the missing word, here 'impious arts', the irreligious wiles that seduced Monmouth's followers.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap needs an adjective meaning irreverent or ungodly, which completes Dryden's line.

clue.text: Rude tale spread about radical Madame Bovary?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagrammed letters go round the abbreviation
spread here means scattered about, so the letters of the two words are laid out afresh

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for radical

explanation.surface: A crude story circulates concerning a political extremist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' gives the anagram ADULTEER, which 'about' wraps round R. The question mark marks Emma Bovary as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaubert's heroine Emma Bovary betrays her husband with two lovers, so she is an example of a faithless spouse.

clue.text: When Talos might finally write his will as a novel?

definitions.text: When Talos might finally write his will as a novel?

parts.words: When Talos might finally write his will as a novel?
parts.note: the setter imagines leaving his will to the very last moment, on his deathbed, and the phrase for that moment is also the title of a Faulkner novel

explanation.walkthrough: Faulkner's 1930 novel follows the Bundren family carrying their mother's body to burial; its first-person title doubles as the moment of the setter's imagined deathbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A will written at the last moment is written on one's deathbed, which matches the first-person title of Faulkner's novel.

clue.text: British man getting hard time about Jesus

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole string of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: a man is a male
H stands for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A British man is serving a long jail sentence for something concerning Christ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole run BMALEHT back to front. 'Hard time' looks like a prison sentence but is two separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ is called the Lamb of God, and Blake's poem of that title addresses him.

clue.text: First piece from Tolstoy with a German title

indicators.note: the first piece of the word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An opening chapter of Tolstoy appears with a German heading.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag is a label or name attached to something, as a title is.

clue.text: & 15: Zoo ideal to be made over by wee common woman

indicators.note: to be made over means to be remodelled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: wee is Scots for little

explanation.surface: A perfect zoo is to be renovated by a humble lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be made over' rearranges ZOO IDEAL into ELIZADOO, followed by LITTLE. Shaw's Pygmalion flower girl is the common woman made over into a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's Cockney flower seller in Pygmalion is the archetypal working-class woman transformed by Higgins.

clue.text: A-list with a pair of liberals and The Great Golden Onos?

annotationWithheld.why: A-list with a pair of liberals and The Great Golden Onos? (3-4): A + LL gives the start of ALL-STAR, but no reading of 'The Great Golden Onos' (possibly a misprint) honestly yields STAR or defines the answer
annotationWithheld.clue: A-list with a pair of liberals and The Great Golden Onos?

clue.text: Albatross by Fleetwood Mac? It's about World War One!

definitions.meaning: Fleetwood Mac's Albatross is a piece of music named after a seabird, so jokingly a seabird's tune
Sebastian Faulks's novel of that name is set in the trenches of the First World War

explanation.surface: A Fleetwood Mac hit turns out to be a song about the Great War.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: an instrumental named after a seabird is a seabird's tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Faulks's 1993 novel follows Stephen Wraysford through the Somme; and a seabird's music is a tune sung by a feathered creature.

clue.text: Will Harmon be doing it for high rating and cup?

definitions.text: Will Harmon be doing it for high rating and cup?

parts.words: Will Harmon be doing it for high rating and cup?
parts.note: Beth Harmon, the chess prodigy of Tevis's The Queen's Gambit, takes opponents' pieces to raise her rating and win trophies

explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is the future tense, not a first name: Harmon is Beth Harmon of The Queen's Gambit, and taking pieces is what wins her games.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, taking an opponent's piece is the act needed to win games, ratings and cups.

clue.text: Fish rector nets close to pal Bartleby, perhaps

indicators.note: nets means catches, so the fish-and-rector pair takes in a letter

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A clergyman catches fish beside his friend Bartleby.
explanation.walkthrough: Melville's Bartleby the Scrivener 'would prefer not to' work, so he is an example of a layabout.
explanation.definitionFit: Melville's scrivener refuses all work, making him an example of a shirker or loafer.

clue.text: Around foremost of readers, promote failed Sci-fi writer

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the synonym for promote goes about a letter

parts.note: to tout is to promote or advertise

indicators.note: the foremost part of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A publicist pushes an unsuccessful science-fiction author on the leading readers.
explanation.walkthrough: Kilgore Trout is Kurt Vonnegut's recurring hack science-fiction writer, whose books sell nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Vonnegut's Kilgore Trout is a prolific but unsuccessful pulp science-fiction author.

clue.text: "I had rather be a beggar's dog than -" (Shakespeare)

definitions.text: "I had rather be a beggar's dog than -" (Shakespeare)

parts.words: "I had rather be a beggar's dog than -" (Shakespeare)
parts.note: a line from Timon of Athens with the name gapped: Alcibiades's insult names the play's churlish philosopher

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: in Timon of Athens the cynic philosopher is so disliked that a beggar's dog is preferred to him.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap needs the name of Timon's cynical, abusive philosopher companion in the play.

clue.text: Children's writer making edits, then it is bed

indicators.note: making edits means reworking text, so the letters of the following words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An author revises her manuscript and then retires for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making edits' rearranges THEN IT IS BED. 'edits' itself is no fodder: it tells you to edit.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Nesbit wrote The Railway Children and Five Children and It, classics of children's fiction.

clue.text: Girl stranded in Barking might pick this author up

definitions.text: Girl stranded in Barking might pick this author up

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so letters in that state are jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl stuck in the east London suburb of Barking might pick up a book by this author.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, but 'barking' also means mad, the anagram signal for GIRL STRANDED. A stranded girl might read Pippi Longstocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrid Lindgren created Pippi Longstocking, so a girl at a loose end might pick up her books.

clue.text: See 6
Stupid to let in "Charlie" like Dougal Douglas?

indicators.note: to let in means to admit, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: sottish means stupid with drink
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: It's foolish to admit a man called Charlie who resembles Dougal Douglas.
explanation.walkthrough: Dougal Douglas is the mischievous Scot in Muriel Spark's The Ballad of Peckham Rye.
explanation.definitionFit: Spark's Dougal Douglas is an Edinburgh-born incomer to London, so being from north of the border describes him.

clue.text: Drinks brought over at the same time as memoir

parts.note: cider is an apple drink
with can mean at the same time as, as in rising with the sun
Rosie Lee is rhyming slang for tea, shortened to rosie

explanation.surface: Drinks are served at the same moment that a memoir is published.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosie, short for Rosie Lee, is British rhyming slang for tea, so the one word 'Drinks' supplies two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurie Lee's book recounts his boyhood in a Cotswold village and is a classic autobiography.

clue.text: Padre is erring holding Jennie Gerhardt's father

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the run of letters is concealed in the words

explanation.surface: A chaplain errs while keeping Jennie Gerhardt's dad in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' looks like a parent or priest, chiming with 'Padre', but here it means the novel's creator.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Dreiser wrote the novel Jennie Gerhardt, so he is its creator, figuratively its parent.

clue.text: Island king heading up Italy to find Max Brod eventually?

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An island monarch travels north to Italy in search of Max Brod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading up' turns LEAR to RAEL. Max Brod, Kafka's friend, fled Prague in 1939 and settled in Tel Aviv.
explanation.definitionFit: Brod emigrated to Palestine and became a citizen of the new Jewish state, so by the end of his life he was its national.

clue.text: Article at work sent up Talos' pen name

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
on means working, as a machine is on

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the setter Talos speaking of himself would say my

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece at the office mocks the setter's pseudonym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' looks like mockery but reverses MY to YM. The setter's name stands for 'my', the setter's own possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: An anonym is an assumed or concealed name, like a pseudonym.

clue.text: Philosophical novel that's likely to go viral?

definitions.meaning: Camus's 1947 novel set in Oran during an epidemic is a work of existential philosophy
humorously, an epidemic disease is something that spreads widely, like an online post going viral

explanation.surface: A novel of ideas seems set to become an internet sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go viral' usually means spreading online; here it is literal, a disease spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: Camus's existentialist work is named after the epidemic it depicts, and a pestilence spreads by infection.

clue.text: Parts of poetry can be a chore for schoolkids

definitions.meaning: verses are made up of these rows of words

definitions.text: can be a chore for schoolkids
definitions.meaning: a written punishment given to pupils, copying out a sentence many times

explanation.surface: Learning verse can be a tiresome task for pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a punishment of writing the same sentence over and over is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Poems are written in rows of verse, and the school punishment of repeated writing shares the name.

clue.text: One managed to arrest male spy from the subcontinent

indicators.note: to arrest means to hold or catch, so the pair of pieces holds a letter

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
ran means managed, as one runs a business

explanation.surface: A man in charge is told to detain a male Indian agent.
explanation.walkthrough: Ali Imran is the secret-agent hero of Ibn-e-Safi's Urdu Imran Series of spy novels from Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibn-e-Safi's Urdu thrillers star a South Asian secret agent of that name.

clue.text: Brand writer one with rubbish erotic novel primarily

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
BS is a slang abbreviation for rubbish

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so the opening letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: A writer of a brand teams up with a trashy erotic novel above all.
explanation.walkthrough: Brand is Ibsen's 1865 verse play about an uncompromising priest, not a commercial brand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian dramatist wrote the verse play Brand, so he is its author.

clue.text: Woe Genet suffered acquiring book for Leo Colston?

indicators.note: acquiring means taking in, so the anagram gains a letter inside it
suffered means went through distress, so the letters are churned up

explanation.surface: Jean Genet's misery deepens as he acquires a book for Leo Colston.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffered' gives the anagram GOETWEEN, which takes B inside it. In L.P. Hartley's novel Leo Colston carries letters between two lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hartley's novel young Leo carries secret letters between two lovers, acting as their messenger.

clue.text: Was able to pick up good books

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone managed to collect some fine reading material.
explanation.definitionFit: To have got something is to have understood it, to have managed to take it in.

clue.text: Description of the Corleones is very determined

definitions.meaning: the Godfather's mafia family is a tough group of people, a ruthless crowd
firmly fixed and unbending in purpose

explanation.surface: The Godfather's family are portrayed as utterly resolute.
explanation.walkthrough: The Corleones are the mafia family of Mario Puzo's The Godfather.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fixed and unyielding in purpose is firmly settled, rigid in resolve; a tough mob family is a tough crowd.

clue.text: Those people circling tree in tale of Mitch McDeere

indicators.note: circling means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: them means those people
a fir is a coniferous tree

explanation.surface: A group of people encircle a tree in a story about Mitch McDeere.
explanation.walkthrough: Mitch McDeere is the young lawyer hero of John Grisham's legal thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Grisham's thriller follows McDeere as he joins a corrupt Memphis law practice.
